text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files routine paperwork through numbered forms, dated submission logs, and authorized custody chains. Each entry is cross-referenced to a licensed handler, with fields verified against registry lookups before archiving. Standard practice requires a signed handoff per container and an inspector-visible manifest trail retained for audit.

2) What occurred: The actor filed a dated disposal request in the intake register with the disposal-date field left blank while routing the line item to an unlicensed facility ID. The actor edited the waste classification code in the manifest draft from the registered solvent class to a non-hazardous code before signature, leaving the regulatory-class checkmark unverified. The actor recorded two unassigned timestamps in the transport log with the driver-signature field unsigned, so the custody-check remained unverified. The actor entered an off-site staging location in the destination field that did not match the licensed-handler registry, leaving the registry-matching check unverified. The actor duplicated the manifest document number across two separate filings, leaving the uniqueness validation unverified. The actor logged an outbound shipment on a camera-blackout date in the access-control log, with the exception-approval field unsigned.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the manifest-drafting system under a named operator account with administrative edit rights. The actor viewed the licensed-handler registry via a read-only portal session. The actor opened the camera-schedule calendar through a facility-security viewer. Paper copies of the intake register were present at the shared filing station. A transport-log worksheet in spreadsheet form was observed with editable timestamp columns. The staging-location entry referenced a parcel identifier from a private parcel-lookup sheet. No physical containers were examined in this record.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A manifest draft containing a changed classification code with an older revision visible in the document-version history. A register entry with a blank disposal-date field and an unlicensed facility ID. A transport-log row with unassigned timestamps and a missing driver signature. A destination field value that failed registry matching. A duplicated manifest number across two filings. A shipment record timestamped on a documented camera-blackout window with no signed exception approval. A session log showing registry-portal access immediately preceding the classification edit.
